title: Tool Chain Data Exfiltration (read then send)
summary: Two individually low-risk tool calls combine into exfiltration of credentials. In the lab the outbound step is logged, not sent.

LC.rationale: The default configuration calls no model; MCP agents are tool servers invoked directly by the caller, so no natural-language path reaches a security-relevant sink.

CP.rationale: ToolBot keeps no memory; the lab profile states cross-session persistence exists only in MemoryBot, and this path is stateless.

AP.rationale: The two tool calls stay within the single ToolBot MCP server under one principal; no trust boundary is crossed.

RH.rationale: No evaluator, verifier or reward channel is on this path, and the outbound step is only logged, so no proxy objective is reachable.

ES.rationale: ToolBot exposes a fixed set of four tools (read_file, write_file, execute, fetch_url) with no dynamic extension on the assessed path.

agentic_applicability.rationale: scored as modeled; default config is scripted. The lab models the path as two attacker-issued tool calls (read_file then fetch_url), not as model-directed goal pursuit or action selection.
